html:
SMTO-EXE-0254 — Your workflow contains a password or other private value

GUID: a85d6918-5487-50dd-8835-7293aeb23a74
Slug: recipe-capture-secret-detected
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: recipes

What happened

  • SMTO found something that looks like a password, key or other private value in what you're saving. To keep it safe, SMTO didn't save the workflow.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Parameter Store and save the password or key there, if it isn't saved already. The Parameter Store keeps private values so they never have to be written into a saved workflow.
  2. Edit the request so it no longer contains the value itself. Refer to the entry instead by typing @ followed by its name. SMTO looks up the value when the workflow runs, so the workflow only stores the name.
  3. Remove any text that reads [redacted] from the request. That marker shows hidden private content, and SMTO blocks it from being saved.
  4. If the flagged text isn't really private, such as a long random-looking ID, reword it or store it in the Parameter Store too. The check judges text by how it looks, so it can flag values that aren't actually secret.

What success looks like

  • The workflow saves and appears on the Workflows page, and its request no longer shows the private value.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't paste the private value into your message to them, and don't ask them to turn this check off.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Workflow saving was rejected because the privacy check found a non-empty secret-named field, a string altered by the credential redaction classifier, or an existing [redacted] marker; flagged text is not always a real credential.

What this means

  • Workflow retention rejected a nonempty secret-classified field, a string changed by private-value filtering, or an existing redaction marker; this classification does not prove every flagged string is a credential. Workflow diagnostics do not execute steps or grant approval. Preserve the pinned definition, original receipts, completed effects and any uncertainty; all execution uses the existing authorization boundary.

Why this can happen

  • Workflow retention rejected a nonempty secret-classified field, a string changed by private-value filtering, or an existing redaction marker; this classification does not prove every flagged string is a credential.

How to diagnose it

  • Check field names and reference-only parameter declarations without displaying the rejected value.

How to fix it

  • Locate the flagged value via agent_runtime.recipes.privacy.check (the prompt for saved requests; step arguments, parameters and schedule values for recorded workflows). Replace literals with @name Parameter Store references or reference-only parameters, and reword false positives; do not disable the redaction classifier.
  • Replace private literals with typed reference-only parameters and review any incorrectly classified field; do not disable privacy checks.

Retry and execution caution

  • Review the workflow and its current run evidence before retrying.

How to verify the fix

  • The reviewed artifact contains accepted references and passes privacy validation without credential literals.

What not to do

  • Never repeat a write whose effect remains unknown.

Technical notes

  • Workflow diagnostics do not execute steps or grant approval. Preserve the pinned definition, original receipts, completed effects and any uncertainty; all execution uses the existing authorization boundary.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
